stamp: {"keys":[{"id":"k","problem":"A fund the reader added gets labels ('צוברת', 'חשיפה לדולר') that the reader never gave, and the reader cannot choose its labels.","where":"the added fund's row in the fund list","kind":"general"}],"liked":[]}

raised: The main fund list doesn't price the reader's own fund ('עוד לא נאסף', 'אין מחיר כאן').
The 'סוג קרן אחר' table puts the Swap fund 19,980 ₪ worse, about 22,000 ₪ from the similar Core fund, with no explanation; the 'כלל מס פתוח' lock reads as unsettled tax and worries them.
The Swap fund and Core share the same ID code IE00B5BMR087, so the page may be looking at the wrong fund.
The coloured cost bar has too many colours.
The coloured tags in the fund list are too many to read on every row.
The long 'לא בחישוב' notes about soldiers and students don't apply to them.
The Interactive Brokers box prices the Core fund, not theirs, so it's only half useful.
The list of complaints (טענות) made them trust the advertised prices less.
The 'מה הכי משנה' chart is common sense and doesn't help choose a fund.
The currency-hedging section confused them, and its 4-year base is too small to rely on.
The step chart starts from MTF at Jerusalem ('עכשיו'), which they never told the page and don't hold.
Unclear whether the 'מול המדד' column (+0.37%) is good or bad.
They don't understand what '4D' and '4A' mean in fund names.
They don't understand what 'מס גם על שינוי המטבע' means in shekels compared with 'מס רק במכירה'.
Unclear who the trustee in 'נאמן 0.02%' is and whether that is paid on top.
No clear line showing their own fund's end amount with a broker next to the winner.
Can't find which Israeli account can buy their fund and what it costs there.
No plain explanation of the tax on a swap fund held from Israel.
Unclear whether their 0.05% fee was used in the 59,196 ₪ figure.
Nothing about safety if the foreign broker or the fund company goes bust.

problems.why: The reader accepts the 'חשיפה לדולר' tag on their fund and only complains that the tags in general are too many; they never say the fund got labels they didn't give or that they can't choose its labels.

raised: The main fund list doesn't price my fund; it shows only 'עוד לא נאסף' / 'אין מחיר כאן'.
One bottom table puts my fund 19,980 ₪ worse, while the similar Core fund comes out better, and I can't see why they're about 22,000 ₪ apart.
The lock note 'כלל מס פתוח' makes the tax on my fund sound uncertain, which worries me.
My fund shows the same ID code (IE00B5BMR087) as iShares Core, so the page may not be looking at the fund I mean.
The coloured cost bar has too many colours.
The fund list has too many coloured tags to read on every row.
The long 'לא בחישוב' notes about soldiers and students don't apply to me.
The Interactive Brokers box prices the Core fund, not mine, so it's only half useful.
The 'מה הכי משנה' chart states the obvious and doesn't help me choose a fund.
The currency-hedging section and its charts are confusing and rest on only 4 years of data.
The step chart starts from MTF at Jerusalem as 'עכשיו', which I never told the page.
It's unclear whether a bigger figure in the 'מול המדד' column is good or bad.
I don't know what '4D' and '4A' mean in the fund names.
I don't understand what 'מס גם על שינוי המטבע' vs 'מס רק במכירה' means in shekels.
It's unclear who the trustee in 'נאמן 0.02%' is and whether I pay that on top.
There's no single clear line showing my own fund's result next to the winner.
The page doesn't say which Israeli account can buy my fund or what it costs there.
There's no plain explanation of the tax on a swap fund held from Israel.
It's unclear whether my 0.05% fee was used in the 59,196 ₪ figure.
There's nothing on safety if the foreign broker or the fund company goes bust.

problems.why: The reader treats the 'חשיפה לדולר' tag as a true fact about their fund and never complains that the page added labels they didn't give or that they can't choose them; the ID-code complaint is about something else.
